issue: The drawn roofline is inconsistent with its labeled ridge (~295) and peak (1e15 FLOP/s): the black memory-bound segment starts at ~1e12 FLOP/s at AI=1 and reaches 1e15 at ~295, which implies bandwidth ~1e12 B/s and ridge ~1000, not ~295. The decode marker at AI~1, ~3e12 FLOP/s therefore sits above the drawn roof.
evidence: Axes: x 'arithmetic intensity (FLOP/byte)' 1..10000; y 'attainable performance (FLOP/s)' 1e11..1e15. Black line starts at (1,1e12), corner at red dashed 'roofline ridge ~295' and flat roof 1e15. Caption: 'decode at ~1 FLOP/byte' and '~295 ridge'. Roofline formula: attainable = min(peak, B*AI); B = peak/ridge = 1e15/295 ≈ 3.39e12 B/s, so at AI=1 the roof is ~3.39e12, not 1e12. The red decode dot is plotted at ~3e12, above the drawn line.
acceptance_test: Recompute B from the stated peak and ridge; redraw the memory-bound segment through (1, B) and (ridge, peak) with slope 1 on log-log axes; place the decode marker on or below the roof (or replace it with a non-quantitative regime label); verify no marker lies above the roof and that the ridge label matches the drawn corner.

issue: The Token IDs box says 'integers order = position', which conflates token identity with positional encoding. Token IDs are vocabulary indices; position IDs are assigned separately and encoded by the model.
evidence: Label in the Token IDs box: 'integers / order = position'. The caption says 'text → tokenizer → IDs → embedding → attention' and does not mention position IDs. A reader can infer that the integer token ID encodes its position.
acceptance_test: Replace the label with 'integers; sequence order preserved' and add a separate 'position IDs' annotation on the path to the transformer/attention, or explicitly state that positions are assigned separately. Verify no arrow or label implies token ID = position.

issue: The arrow from Embedding to Attention is labeled 'attend', and the Attention box says 'computes Q, K, V for this token vs all past tokens'. This conflates the projection that produces Q/K/V with the attention operation and can imply that the embedding itself attends or that K/V for past tokens are recomputed.
evidence: Arrow label 'attend' between 'Embedding' and 'Attention'; Attention box text 'computes Q, K, V for this token vs all past tokens'; KV Cache box says 'read + write per layer × head' and the return arrow is labeled 'read past K,V'.
acceptance_test: Relabel the Embedding→Attention arrow 'project Q/K/V' or 'hidden state'; change the Attention box to 'Q from this token; attend over cached past K/V' (or equivalent). Keep 'attend' only for the attention operation, not the embedding transition.

issue: The diagram visually separates token1 ('sampled by prefill') from token2/3 and routes token1 into the top of 'append K/V', which can imply that prefill writes token1's K/V. The caption says a token's K/V is written when it is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled.
evidence: Token1 box: 'token1 / sampled by prefill'; token2: 'first decode output'; token3: 'second decode output'. All feed 'append K/V per layer-head'. Caption: 'written when that token is next processed as input, one step after it is sampled.'
acceptance_test: Add a step boundary or label the token1 path 'appended on first decode' and make the token1/2/3 entry paths visually uniform; verify the figure alone does not imply prefill appends token1's K/V.

issue: Secondary labels are set in small, low-contrast gray type below the 8 pt print floor: 'sampled by prefill', 'first decode output', 'second decode output', 'store K', 'store V', 'read V', 'read K'.
evidence: Rendered page at 150 dpi: these labels are visibly smaller and lighter than the box titles; at print size they are difficult to read, especially in grayscale.
acceptance_test: Increase these labels to at least 8 pt and darken to a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the background; verify at 100% print size and in grayscale.

issue: The 'read' path from the persistent KV cache to the decode transformer is drawn as a plain vertical line without a visible arrowhead, while the 'append' path has a clear upward arrowhead. The direction of the read path is therefore ambiguous.
evidence: Between 'PERSISTENT KV CACHE' and the DECODE transformer: left vertical line labeled 'read' has no visible arrowhead; right vertical line labeled 'append' has an upward arrowhead. Caption: 'each step reads the cached K/V, appends the new K/V'.
acceptance_test: Add a downward arrowhead to the 'read' path and make the read/append pair visually symmetric; verify the direction is unambiguous without relying on the caption.
